source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.section: Tropical, Equinoctial, Fixed, and Bicorporeal Signs
source_locator.short_quote: The tropical signs are two ... the sign of Cancer ... and the sign of Capricorn.

calculation_dependencies: sign position after summer or winter solstice

condition.source_definition: first thirty degrees after the summer or winter solstice

normalized_rule: Classify Cancer and Capricorn as the tropical signs, beginning with the thirty degrees after the summer and winter solstices respectively.
synthesis_notes: This is a source-specific sign taxonomy, not an astronomical claim about modern zodiac boundaries.
review_notes: Keep the four sign-category rules separate and preserve the source's tropical-point terminology.
transmission_notes: The category and sign assignments are explicit in the Ashmand/Proclus main text. They are not replaced by later sign-modality conventions.
